lhs: Apply exp to scalar zero or the pointwise constant zero tensor.
rhs: Pointwise constant one at the original shape.
conditions: Direct rank-zero literal or immediate broadcast of that literal. Exact zero input, arbitrary valid broadcast output shape, no fast-math gate.
types: Homogeneous exact real or complex logical tensors.
overlap: Two constructors instantiate one existing constant-function identity family.

conditions: Both multiply operands are the same Abs instruction; its input is noncomplex. The selected model restricts the element type to exact reals.
types: Homogeneous exact real tensor at arbitrary shape.
overlap: Historical real identity. No concluded integer-overflow or encoded floating profile.

conditions: Source fast math enabled and both operands Exp. On the exact real/complex model there is no positivity, range, or principal-log condition.
types: Same-shaped homogeneous exact real or complex tensors.
overlap: Historical exponential addition identity family; fast math is source admission, not a mathematical axiom or a guarantee about rounding.

lhs: Bitcast dense cells to the same shape and layout.
conditions: Static untiled same element type, identical layout, dimensions and cell count; no control dependencies and compatible replacement metadata.
overlap: Identical-layout partition of the historical cell-read/write law.

rhs: One bitcast with the original input and final output shape/layout.
conditions: The two-bitcast pattern still matches after recursion on the inner instruction. Both steps preserve element count in their three dense views; no outer control dependencies.
types: Same fixed cell type, static untiled shapes, arbitrary ranks.
overlap: Historical cancellation of the intermediate storage view. The later compatible-stage is a separate test.

conditions: One-operand, one-user, nonfusion elementwise instruction with same element type across all nodes and untiled inner bitcast and inner operand. Here the unary is a pure shape-independent cell function and all views are dense untiled with matching cell counts.
types: Same fixed element type throughout, static dense logical tensors.
overlap: Historical map transport plus composition. Op-dependent effects and tiled outer views excluded.

lhs: Bitcast-convert identically typed words at the same shape.
conditions: Same logical shape, word width and bit order. The physical theorem additionally needs the same dense layout. Final compatibility branch reached after earlier rewrites decline.
types: Homogeneous fixed-width words on static arrays.
overlap: Existing logical identity and equal-layout physical specialization. Neither requires ignoring observable layout differences.

lhs: Transpose by the specified output-to-input permutation.
rhs: Physical same-cell bitcast into the transpose output view.
conditions: Layout-sensitive source; both layouts assigned; output extents permute the input extents and composition of the permutation with output minor-to-major equals input minor-to-major. Untiled, equal-byte-size, same-cell-type profile. Earlier transpose branches decline.
types: Static untiled dense arrays at arbitrary rank.
overlap: Existing certified dense transpose theorem. Tiled size and layout policy remain outside this profile.

lhs: Observe the row-major to column-major same-width physical reinterpretation at coordinate (0,1).
rhs: Delete the operation and observe the unchanged logical input at (0,1).
conditions: Explicit dense 2×2 U8 layouts, row-major input x(i,j)=10*i+j and column-major result. Layout-insensitive compatibility, unsharded parameter, no control edges. Fix physical input/output views for this evaluator-profile observation.
types: Static U8 words at identical numeric shape.
overlap: One historical physical-layout counterexample; same-width theorem connects cell bitcast with word reinterpretation. No new native execution or general abstract HLO disproof.

conditions: Static rank-three forward CPU convolution, F32 input, BF16 kernel/result, base dilation 2 on length two, unit-width kernel, no groups beyond one, parameter operands; oneDNN enabled, earlier folds/swap disabled or inapplicable. Finite integer-valued inputs through 511 and filters through 15, BF16 ties to even, exact F32 intermediate values.
lhs: Convert input to BF16 result type, widen into F32 convolution arithmetic and convert output back to BF16.
rhs: Widen operands directly to F32, convolve, then convert output to BF16.
types: F32 × BF16 with BF16 result, numerical equality on these integer-valued inputs.
overlap: The source swaps early and late rounding on an operand. A separate dot-strength counterexample depended on rounding a product. No native execution or generic low-precision backend verdict.
